newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends up on A share rises.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends up on A share rises.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended up on Monday on a rebound due to speculative domestic buying in low-priced shares encouraged by sharp rises on the A share market, brokers said.
The B share index was up 0.591 points or 0.81 percent to 73.527 points on volume of 17.5 million shares worth $7.6 million compared with $6.3 million last Friday.
The A share index rose 34.045 points or 2.7 percent to 1,293.362 points on turnover of nine billion yuan.
Brokers said prevailing rumours of financial restructuring stirred active buying in low-priced shares with poor results records.

"Low-priced shares were the focus of the market today, with domestic investors speculating amid unfounded rumours," one broker said. But the speculative buying was high-risk as the cheap counters had no fundamental support, he said.
"The B market will follow the movements on the A share market as domestic investors dominate trading in the short term," another broker said.
All 43 B shares traded with 30 up, six flat and seven down.
Shanghai Vacuum & Electron Device was the star on speculative buying, rising $0.018 or 7.82 percent to $0.248 on volume of 1.1 million shares.
Bicycle maker Shanghai Phoenix followed, also on speculative buying, gaining $0.014 or 7.52 percent to $0.200 on volume of 1.6 million shares.
Toy maker Shanghai Haixin traded the most on profit-taking after sharp gains in the past few days, falling $0.006 or 0.93 percent to $0.638 on volume of 2.1 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index ended sharply up on active speculative buying in selected stocks, brokers said.
The SSE 30 blue chip index gained 34.144 points or 1.01 percent to 3418.278 points.
Among the nine A shares to surge 10 percent to their limit-up, Shanghai Zhongxi Pharmaceutical rose 1.16 yuan to 12.72 yuan on volume of 2.1 million shares, also on speculative buying.
